key_insight: By combining photoluminescence imaging with drift-diffusion modeling and Bayesian inference, the study maps where perovskite solar cells degrade and identifies whether the dominant failure originates at the hole or electron transport interface, or in the bulk.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical diagnostic framework for targeting stability fixes in perovskite solar cells, helping engineers design more durable devices and validate passivation strategies.
method: Photoluminescence imaging collected spatially resolved signals from fully fabricated devices.
Drift-diffusion simulations were paired with Bayesian inference to infer recombination-related parameter maps.
Parameter maps were tracked during accelerated aging at 70 °C under full-spectrum sunlight to localize degradation pathways.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports pronounced spatial heterogeneity in inferred optoelectronic maps during aging, with the strongest degradation concentrated near perovskite/transport-layer interfaces and reduced by amino-silane passivation.
watch_item: The inferred maps depend on model assumptions and the fidelity of the drift-diffusion/Bayesian framework, so incorrect priors or missing physics could bias attribution of degradation pathways.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
